name: Health Information Management
description: The discipline that owns the medical record — its completeness, its accuracy, its legal standing, its privacy, and the coded data every hospital's reporting and reimbursement runs on. ⚠⚠⚠ This is the ONE route in the health-information family that leads to the field's professional credentials, because RHIT eligibility requires an ASSOCIATE DEGREE from a CAHIIM-accredited programme. Taught at 31 Florida public institutions.
degreesNote: ⚠⚠⚠ THE ACCREDITATION IS THE PRODUCT. AHIMA's rule for the RHIT examination is that you must have completed the academic requirements, at associate degree level, of a Health Information Management programme accredited by CAHIIM — the Commission on Accreditation for Health Informatics and Information Management Education. ⚠⚠ A certificate does not qualify, however good it is, and ⚠⚠⚠ AHIMA states that HEALTH INFORMATICS degrees are NOT currently accepted for RHIT either. That is the trap worth knowing before you enrol: a degree whose name sounds newer and more technical can leave you unable to sit the examination the field hires on. Ask the programme for its CAHIIM accreditation and check it with CAHIIM. ⚠ Florida awards 296 credentials a year across these codes — 169 under health information technology (109 of them associate degrees) and 127 under the administration code, which is the bachelor's-level RHIA route. ⚠⚠ Read the course numbers as the map: Florida puts this programme at HIM1xxx and HIM2xxx, which are COLLEGE CREDIT, while the coder/biller certificates sit at HIM0xxx, which are CLOCK HOURS. The level digit is what decides whether the hours can ever become a degree. ⚠ Look for HIM2960, the credentialing examination review course, in a programme's plan — nine institutions list a coding or review capstone and it is a good sign that the programme is aimed at the credential rather than at the certificate.

cips.note: Health Information/Medical Records Technology/Technician — 28 Florida public institutions and 169 credentials, 109 of them ASSOCIATE DEGREES. ⚠ This is the CAHIIM/RHIT route, and the associate degree is what makes it one.

Health Information/Medical Records Administration — only 3 Florida public institutions but 127 credentials, at bachelor's level. ⚠ The RHIA rung above RHIT, and worth knowing it exists at three places before assuming the associate degree is the ceiling.

related.note: ⚠⚠⚠ The route students most often confuse with this one, and the difference decides a career. Billing and coding is taught at 37 Florida institutions against 31 here and awards more credentials — but they are CLOCK-HOUR certificates (HIM0xxx), and a certificate makes nobody RHIT-eligible. ⚠ Coding is a job you can hold with a certificate; health information management is a department you can run with the degree.

⚠ The third route in the same family and the most often mistaken for this one. Medical secretaries and administrative assistants schedule, register, verify insurance and manage the front office; health information staff own the record itself. ⚠⚠ 850,000 people work in the front-office occupation against 194,800 in medical records, so it is the larger job market — but it pays less and has no credential ladder.

⚠ A neighbouring certificate at many of the same institutions, and the comparison worth making if you are deciding between a clinical and an administrative route. Medical assisting has a clinical half — venipuncture, injections, vital signs — that this does not. ⚠ If the idea of drawing blood is the deciding factor, that is a legitimate way to choose between them.

⚠ Not a route, and named for a specific reason: health information departments hire experienced clinicians into clinical documentation improvement and coding audit roles, where knowing what a chart MEANS is worth more than speed. ⚠⚠ It is one of the few desk-based second careers a nurse can move into without starting over, and nobody advertises it.
